annotations.description: Nature's Way is premium green removal in limited, dealing damage equal to a creature's power to an opposing creature. Bottoming it in favor of a small Merfolk creature means giving up one of the stronger removal spells available. While Merfolk Pupil helps with curve and tribal synergies (Crashing Tide flash, Amoeboid Changeling), Nature's Way is harder to replace and more impactful in the mid-to-late game.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Nature's Way on the bottom, keeping Merfolk Pupil on top.
annotations.betterLine: Put Merfolk Pupil on the bottom and keep Nature's Way on top. The player already has Eyekite as a 2-drop, and Nature's Way serves as important removal that's difficult to replace. Early creature density matters less than having answers to opponent's threats.

annotations.description: Passed with 3 untapped lands in postcombat main phase when Crashing Tide was available to bounce the opponent's only creature (Eyekite) and draw a card, or Amoeboid Changeling could be deployed as a body. Crashing Tide especially would be a strong tempo play - removing the opponent's only threat while replacing itself.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, ending the turn with 3 mana unused and no action taken.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Crashing Tide targeting Eyekite to bounce the opponent's only creature and draw a card, gaining significant tempo advantage. Alternatively, cast Amoeboid Changeling to develop the board and enable flash on future Crashing Tides.

annotations.description: At 8 life facing 5 opponent creatures, passed the turn without playing Thriving Isle (land drop) or casting any of the available flash creatures. The opponent's board threatens lethal or near-lethal next attack. Every blocker matters critically here.
